question: What fields define a Kubernetes Toleration, and how do they match node taints?

ground_truth.answer: A Toleration allows a Pod to be scheduled onto a node that has a matching taint. key names the taint key; operator is Exists (tolerates any value for the key) or Equal (value must match); value is the taint value matched when operator is Equal; effect specifies which taint effect to tolerate: NoSchedule (prevents scheduling), PreferNoSchedule (discourages scheduling), or NoExecute (evicts running Pods); an empty effect tolerates all effects. tolerationSeconds applies only to NoExecute and specifies how long the Pod may remain on the tainted node before being evicted. A Toleration with an empty key and operator Exists tolerates all taints.
context: io.k8s.api.core.v1.Toleration: key, operator (Exists/Equal), value, effect (NoSchedule/PreferNoSchedule/NoExecute), and tolerationSeconds fields define taint-toleration matching and eviction behavior
